1. **Outside view.** The series is on a steady, slow downtrend. Weekly deltas over the last 10 releases: −0.7, +0.3, −1.6, −0.1, −1.0, −1.9, 0.0, −0.3, −1.2. Mean ≈ −0.72 per week, sd of the weekly change ≈ 0.7. There is essentially no mean reversion — MRP smoothing makes this a low-noise, autocorrelated drift. Naive extrapolation from 66.8: about 66.1. A slightly longer-window slope (last 4 weeks ≈ −0.85/wk) gives ~65.9.

2. **Inside view.** The Sept 6 NBC story explicitly reports Trump's approval slipping *among Republicans* ahead of the midterms, and the national number is at a term low (Reuters/Ipsos 33%, NBC 36%). That is consistent with the erosion already embedded in this cut rather than a new shock, so it argues against any bounce-back: worth about −0.2 relative to a pure random-walk assumption. No obvious rally-round-the-flag event or intra-party consolidation catalyst in the window; the Iran war and affordability/tariff stories are cutting the other way. Republican floor effects (net can't fall indefinitely; 82% approve/~12% disapprove implies room, but decay slows as the remaining base is the hard core) argue for slight flattening: +0.2. Net effect roughly cancels; center near 66.0.

3. **Pre-mortem.** Most likely way I'm wrong: the decline is not a smooth drift but punctuated — a week of −2.5 (like the 8/07→8/14 move) if a Republican-salient story breaks, or an abrupt flattening/uptick as the model absorbs a burst of favorable partisan responses (there was a +0.3 and two ~0.0 weeks in the sample). Also, Civiqs revises nightly, so the Friday read can shift the prior baseline itself. Correction: don't put the center below ~65.7 (avoid over-extrapolating the steepest recent slope) and widen the sd beyond the raw 0.7 weekly-change sd to cover both retro-revision and jump risk.

4. **Calibrate.** One-sd band of ±1.0 spans roughly 65.0–67.0, which comfortably contains all but the largest observed weekly moves applied to 66.8 (66.8−1.9 = 64.9 at the tail; 66.8+0.3 = 67.1). That feels right for ~two-thirds coverage with fat-ish tails.
